_comment: Figures referenced by events. 'dates' are traditional/scholarly approximations and often debated; treat them as display strings, not precise facts. Mythological/legendary figures are flagged via 'historicity'.

figures.name: Prophet Muhammad
figures.role: Final prophet in Islam; recipient of the Qur'anic revelation
figures.summary: Born in Mecca, Muhammad is regarded in Islam as the last in a line of prophets. His revelations form the Qur'an, and his life in Mecca and Medina anchors much of Islamic sacred geography.

figures.name: Husayn ibn Ali
figures.role: Grandson of Muhammad; central figure in Shia Islam
figures.summary: His death at Karbala in 680 CE is a defining event in Shia Islam, commemorated annually during Muharram.

figures.name: Jesus of Nazareth
figures.role: Central figure of Christianity; also honored as a prophet in Islam
figures.summary: A first-century Jewish teacher whose life and teachings are the foundation of Christianity. Christians believe in his crucifixion and resurrection in Jerusalem.

figures.name: Paul the Apostle
figures.summary: Originally a persecutor of early Christians, his conversion near Damascus and missionary journeys were pivotal in spreading Christianity across the Roman world.

figures.name: Constantine the Great
figures.summary: His reign marked the legalization of Christianity in the Roman Empire and the convening of the First Council of Nicaea in 325 CE.

figures.name: Abraham
figures.role: Patriarch revered across Judaism, Christianity, and Islam
figures.summary: A foundational patriarch in all three Abrahamic faiths. His traditional burial site is the Cave of the Patriarchs in Hebron.

figures.name: Moses
figures.role: Prophet and lawgiver who, in tradition, received the Torah
figures.summary: In Jewish tradition, Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt and received the Torah at Mount Sinai. He is also honored as a prophet in Christianity and Islam.

figures.name: King Solomon
figures.role: King of Israel, builder of the First Temple in tradition
figures.summary: Credited in tradition with building the First Temple in Jerusalem. Honored across the Abrahamic faiths.

figures.name: Krishna
figures.role: Major Hindu deity; central to the Bhagavad Gita
figures.summary: A widely worshipped deity associated with Mathura and Vrindavan. His counsel to Arjuna at Kurukshetra forms the Bhagavad Gita.

figures.name: Rama
figures.role: Major Hindu deity; hero of the Ramayana
figures.summary: A revered deity whose life is told in the Ramayana. Ayodhya is traditionally regarded as his birthplace.

figures.name: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
figures.summary: Born in Lumbini, he attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and taught a path to liberation from suffering across the Ganges plain.

figures.name: Emperor Ashoka
figures.summary: After embracing Buddhism, he spread the tradition across his empire and built numerous stupas, including at Sanchi.

figures.name: Guru Nanak
figures.role: Founder and first Guru of Sikhism
figures.summary: Born in present-day Nankana Sahib, he founded Sikhism and established the community at Kartarpur.

figures.name: Guru Arjan
figures.summary: Compiled the Adi Granth and oversaw completion of the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) in Amritsar.

figures.name: Guru Gobind Singh
figures.role: Tenth and final human Guru of Sikhism
figures.summary: Founded the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib in 1699 and designated the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru.

figures.name: Amaterasu
figures.role: Sun goddess, central kami in Shinto
figures.summary: The sun goddess from whom, in tradition, Japan's imperial line descends. She is enshrined at the Ise Grand Shrine.
